metadata.description: Single-plugin marketplace exposing the cc-enforcer discipline plugin.

plugins.name: cc-enforcer
plugins.description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls rather than asking it nicely. PreToolUse denies an edit before it lands — editing a file you never opened this session, a suppression marker with no adjacent why-comment, a hardcoded secret or user-home path, the fourth small patch to one file, a dangerous shell flag. A nine-layer Stop gate then refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the user's ORIGINAL request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight backed by a hook; "Imperial Edict" regexes you define per project; a repo-wide sync gate; CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the documentation cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, Linux + Windows CI, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.38.3 fixes two defects found by verifying v0.38.2 the way it should be verified — cloning the remote into a fresh directory and running the suite there. Five tests failed while CI was green on the same commit on two platforms, which made 'verification artefact' the obvious conclusion; both were real. The clone sat at a 110-character path and this repository lives at a 23-character one. First: when the contract alone fills the 10,000-character hook cap, build_context dropped every edict and returned SILENTLY, so a session on a deeply-nested install was governed by rules it had never been shown and had no way to learn about — the v0.34.1 defect (all edicts elided, notice reporting 0) living in the sibling branch three releases after the class was supposedly closed. Reproduced first-party across install-root lengths before the fix; the branch now reports the count using the same counter _clip_edicts locates cut points with, because counting twice two ways is how the original notice came to disagree with its own clipper. Second: the header printed the install root twice, and the second copy came out of the budget the header exists to protect — naming it once takes a 300-character root from losing every edict to keeping them. Also a test that sliced the first 200 characters and asserted a filename was inside: true at a 23-character root, false at 110, so it failed on code that was working. It measures the header now. Both fixes verified RED against the pre-fix code, the elision fix with a twin so it cannot degenerate into 'always drop everything and report it'. 738 -> 741 tests. Prior — v0.38.2 takes CLAUDE.md out of the repository. It is the project instruction file Claude Code loads — written for an agent rather than a reader, and its metadata section carries the maintainer's mail address and machine paths. Claude Code reads it from the working tree regardless of git, so untracking costs a local session nothing and a clone simply does not get one. Removing the file was the small half: it was load-bearing in fourteen places — four registered claims in the doc gate, the module-inventory tree, the Bash-deny surface list, the current-release narrative scan, six published links that would have 404'd on the front page, five more in the CHANGELOG, and the release checklist that both READMEs told contributors to go read there. The first attempt made each registry tolerate the file's absence and produced a suite that behaved one way locally and another on CI; that was replaced by a single rule — the doc gates scan the TRACKED repository, link resolution included, so a link to CLAUDE.md fails here exactly as it would in a clone even though the file is on this disk. Verified by running the gate in both states and getting identical results. The release checklist moved into both READMEs' Contributing sections in their own language; the CHANGELOG's references were de-linked but not de-worded, since rewriting what a dated entry says is the falsification the v0.33.0 rename entry refused. A new assertion holds both halves: out of the index AND ignored, because `git rm --cached` alone lets the next `git add -A` put it straight back. 737 -> 738 tests (v0.38.2). Prior — v0.38.1 applies the same rule to the documents v0.38.0 did not look at. A repo-wide scan found the same defect — a Chinese phrase beside its own English translation — in six more English documents, `rules/` among them, which is the English skeleton and the LLM-agnostic product. The rule, applied uniformly: in an English document CJK is allowed only inside a backtick code span, where it is a literal token the reader must type or a detector literally matches. That split the 65 occurrences three ways — 14 DATA tokens backticked rather than deleted (deleting them would make the document false), 51 glosses removed or translated, and one allowed: the language-switcher link, since an English reader needs the Chinese document labelled in Chinese. A gate now holds it — English docs carry no CJK prose, every markdown file is classified as English / Chinese-by-decision / unscanned-with-a-reason, the allowlist must still be needed, and a file registered as Chinese must actually be Chinese so the registry cannot be used to dodge. Verified RED against the pre-sweep tree. 712 -> 737 tests (v0.38.1). Prior — v0.38.0 separates the languages at the source. Everything a guard PRINTS was bilingual — an English body with a Chinese plain-language line appended and Chinese phrasings offered inline — so both READMEs quoted mixed-language samples, and neither could be cleaned without either fabricating output or dropping the samples. The mixing was the product's, not the documentation's. All of that text now lives in a message catalog: `lib/messages_en.py` is the skeleton and source of truth, `lib/messages_zh.py` is its translation, and `lib/messages.py` resolves PER KEY through CC_ENFORCER_LANG, so a partial translation degrades to English rather than blanking a deny. The English half was generated mechanically from the constants the guards carried through v0.37, so the move itself could not change behaviour, and then edited so an English message names the ENGLISH spellings of the markers it describes — checked against the live pattern sets, which accept both languages, so naming only one stays true. Measured end to end: default output now contains zero CJK, and CC_ENFORCER_LANG=zh produces a fully Chinese deny across all seven deny and block paths. i18n_check gained the parity gate the markdown roots cannot have — exact key sets, per-key str.format field sets, and a check that every key a guard asks for exists at all, because a renamed key would otherwise surface as a placeholder marker inside a deny the user is already annoyed by. The status table now pads by display columns rather than code points, which only mattered once a column value could be CJK. 712 -> 733 tests. Prior — v0.37.0 fixes the boundary every single hook invocation passes through. Each entry point read its payload with `sys.stdin.read()`, which decodes with the HOST codepage under the `surrogateescape` error handler — so on any machine whose codepage is not UTF-8 (the default on Windows) the JSON arrived silently rewritten, and every guard scanned a string the agent never wrote. No exception, no stderr, no failing test. Measured on cp936, an em-dash arrived as two characters instead of one, enough to push an inline note past the rule-09 rationale floor and turn a DENY into an ALLOW: the guard was defeated by punctuation. The Stop gate lost far more. `大白话`, `同步核对`, `我觉得` and the done-claim patterns themselves are Chinese, so all of them decoded to mojibake and the CJK half of nine layers matched nothing in production — `_has_done_claim` gates all nine layers and its pattern set is bilingual, so a reply that announced completion only in Chinese matched nothing and skipped the entire stack — measured, a bare completion claim carrying no evidence at all came back allowed with not one layer having fired. Stated precisely rather than loosely, because the looser version would be exactly the overstatement this plugin exists to block: a reply that also said "done" or "fixed" in ASCII still reached layer (a). What it could not do was fail on a Chinese hedge, a Chinese TL;DR marker, or a Chinese sync-check line — those markers were not there to be found. This is the same class the v0.25 `tomlio` hardening closed one boundary over (a wrong decode silently disabling enforcement rather than reporting anything), swept twelve releases late to the boundary that carries every payload. Fixed at the mechanism in a new shared module, `lib/hookio.py`: read stdin's binary buffer, decode UTF-8 strictly per RFC 8259, and let a genuinely malformed payload raise into the existing fail-open handler — loud and diagnosable instead of quietly mangled. Why it survived 691 tests: `tests/_helpers.py` serialised with `json.dumps`, whose `ensure_ascii=True` default escaped every non-ASCII character to a `\uXXXX` sequence before the bytes existed, so the wire was pure ASCII and the decode step had nothing to get wrong — the fixtures could not reach the region the defect lives in, the same shape as the v0.35 `editscale` finding where every fixture happened to be one line long. The harness now puts raw UTF-8 on the wire and a test pins that it does, because restoring the default would re-hide the whole class while leaving everything else green. The end-to-end cases force `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp936:surrogateescape` so a defect that only appears on a non-UTF-8 host still fails on the UTF-8 CI runner, and a vacuity guard fails loudly if that reproduction ever stops biting, so a future Python cannot turn the file green for the wrong reason. Five cases were verified RED against the pre-fix tree; the rest are labelled as controls. 691 -> 712 tests. Full release history: CHANGELOG.md.
